rows.grounds: extends down to the earth principle

items.question: What is the nature of the Shakti principle and its manifest expanse?
premises: In the middle is the pervading goddess Vyāpinī.
In her resides the pervading lord Vyāpīśa, bearer of Vyāpinī.
This level is the Shakti principle, whose manifest expanse extends down to earth.
items.inference: The Shakti principle is the cosmic level where Vyāpinī and Vyāpīśa preside over the entire manifest expanse down to earth.
items.plain_english: In the middle is the pervading goddess Vyāpinī, and in her dwells the pervading lord Vyāpīśa, who bears her. This is the Shakti principle, and its manifest expanse stretches all the way down to the earth principle.

rows.grounds: names the central lord and associated powers

items.question: How are the deities arranged in the Shiva principle?
premises: Above that is the Shiva principle.
In the four directions there are established deities.
At the center is the pervading, sky-natured, infinite lord together with those who share his shakti.
items.inference: The Shiva principle is organized with the infinite sky-natured lord and his shakti-sharers at the center and other deities established in the four directions.
uncertainties: The exact identities of the deities in the four directions are not named in this verse.
items.plain_english: Then comes the Shiva principle. There, deities are established in the four directions, and at the center is the pervading, sky-natured, infinite lord together with those who partake of his shakti.

rows.grounds: describes his radiance and union with shakti

items.question: Who presides at the center of the unsupported level?
premises: In the middle is the unsupported level.
There resides the god of gods, the unsupported one.
He bears his shakti in his lap and shines with the splendor of a billion suns.
items.inference: The unsupported level is presided over by the supreme unsupported god, radiant like a billion suns and united with his shakti.
items.plain_english: In the middle, however, is the unsupported level. There dwells the god of gods, the unsupported one, bearing his shakti in his lap and shining with a splendor equal to a billion suns.

items.question: What is the role of the supreme Shakti above the Shiva principle?
premises: Above the Shiva principle is the supreme Shakti.
She is called Samanā.
She is established as the agent of all causes.
items.inference: Samanā, the supreme Shakti above the Shiva principle, functions as the active agent behind all causes.
items.plain_english: Above the Shiva principle stands the supreme Shakti, called Samanā. She is established as the agent who acts through all causes.

items.question: How do Samanā and Shiva cooperate in cosmic activity?
premises: Presided over by Shiva, Samanā bears many cosmic eggs.
Mounted upon her, Shiva performs the five acts.
Shiva is the lord who carries out this cosmic activity.
items.inference: Samanā sustains the many cosmic eggs under Shiva's presiding power, while Shiva, mounted upon her, performs the five cosmic acts.
items.plain_english: Empowered by Shiva, she bears many cosmic eggs. Mounted upon her, the lord Shiva performs the five cosmic acts.

items.question: How are Samanā and the unsupported principle distinguished as causes?
premises: Samanā is the instrument of the great lord, the causal agent.
The unsupported principle is called the occasioning cause in cosmic activity.
Different causal roles are assigned to Samanā and the unsupported principle.
items.inference: In cosmic activity, Samanā serves as the instrument of the great lord, while the unsupported principle functions as the occasioning cause.
items.plain_english: Samanā is the instrument of the great lord, the causal agent. The unsupported principle, however, is called the occasioning cause in cosmic activity.

items.question: How does the all-pervading lord preside over the five causes?
premises: Through Samanā the all-pervading lord presides.
He presides over the five causes.
He always presides over the unsupported lord Ananta, whose body is space.
items.inference: The all-pervading lord, through Samanā, continually presides over the five causes and over the unsupported lord Ananta, whose body is space.
uncertainties: The exact identity of the five causes is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: Through her the all-pervading lord presides over the five causes, and he always presides over this unsupported lord Ananta, whose body is space.

items.question: How does the supreme lord set the lower powers into motion?
premises: He impels the pervading one by his own shakti.
Below, as an instrument, stands māyā in the form of action.
Below that is the coiled shakti, kuṇḍalinī.
items.inference: The supreme lord impels the pervading one through his own shakti, while māyā functions below as the instrument of action and kuṇḍalinī lies below that.
items.plain_english: He impels the pervading one by his own shakti. Below, māyā stands as the instrument in the form of action, and below that is the coiled shakti, kuṇḍalinī.

items.question: What range of manifestation is described as arising from nāda, bindu, and related principles?
premises: Nāda, bindu, and so forth are described as effects giving rise to the world.
This domain extends upward to Sadāśiva.
This domain extends downward to the earth principle, according to the teaching.
items.inference: The teaching presents nāda, bindu, and related principles as the source of a manifest domain stretching from Sadāśiva down to earth.
items.plain_english: Nāda, bindu, and the rest are the effects through which the world arises. In this teaching, that whole domain extends upward to Sadāśiva and downward to the earth principle.

rows.grounds: subject to arising and passing away

items.question: How is the manifest domain classified, and what topic is introduced next?
premises: All that manifest domain is declared to be derived from prakriti.
It is subject to origination and destruction.
The author now turns to the measure of all the worlds as taught by his own gurus.
items.inference: The manifest domain from Sadāśiva down to earth is classified as prākṛta and impermanent, and the text now moves to explain the measure of all the worlds.
items.plain_english: All of that is declared to be derived from prakriti and subject to arising and destruction. Now I will explain the measure of all the worlds, just as it was taught to me by my own gurus.

items.question: What initial elements of the world-measure are introduced for contemplation?
premises: The measure of the worlds will be explained briefly for understanding.
The explanation enables one to pass quickly through the cosmic egg in contemplation.
Within the egg are Ananta, Kāla, Kūṣmāṇḍa and Hāṭaka, and Brahmā and Hari.
items.inference: The text begins its brief world-measure by listing Ananta, Kāla, Kūṣmāṇḍa, Hāṭaka, Brahmā, and Hari within the cosmic egg.
uncertainties: Kūṣmāṇḍa and Hāṭaka may refer to worlds or regions; the verse names them without explicit category labels.
items.plain_english: That will now be explained briefly, so that one may quickly pass through it in understanding. Within the cosmic egg are Ananta, Kāla, Kūṣmāṇḍa and Hāṭaka, and Brahmā and Hari.

items.question: How many worlds belong to the nivritti level and how are they distributed?
premises: There are a hundred Rudras together with their attendant heroes.
Outside is the nivritti level, which has one hundred and eight worlds.
These are distributed across the seven principles beginning with water, fire, wind, space, ego, and intellect.
items.inference: The nivritti level contains one hundred and eight worlds distributed across the seven lower principles, and it is associated with a hundred Rudras and their attendants.
uncertainties: The verse gives six members of the sevenfold group explicitly; the seventh is implied by 'mūlasaptake' but not named in the surface text.
items.plain_english: There are a hundred Rudras with their attendant heroes. Outside lies the nivritti level, which has one hundred and eight worlds, distributed across the seven principles beginning with water, fire, wind, space, ego, and intellect.
